t: The set of elements that differ in mutual relationship from those of the other sets is:
s:
The correct answer is (D) Li−Na.

Concept:
In the periodic table, certain pairs of diagonally adjacent elements of the second and third periods show similar chemical properties due to comparable ionic sizes and charge-to-radius ratios (polarizing power). This phenomenon is known as a diagonal relationship. 

Options (A) Li−Mg, (B) B−Si, and (C) Be−Al all represent well-known pairs showing this diagonal relationship across different groups. 

In contrast, Li and Na are elements of the same vertical column (Group 1, alkali metals) and therefore exhibit a standard group relationship, making this pair differ from the rest.

t: Give the correct order of initials true (T) or false (F) for given hypothetical species X⁺,X and X⁻: A. Z-effective decreases from X⁺to X⁻ B. Radii increases from X⁻to X⁺ C. Ionisation enthalpy increases from X⁻to X⁺ D. Electronegative decreases from X⁺to X⁻
s: A true (Z_(eff) per electron decreases as electrons are added). B false (radius increases from X⁺ to X⁻, not from X⁻ to X⁺). C true. D true. So T F T T.

The 1​ˢᵗ, 2​ⁿᵈ and the 3​ʳᵈ ionization enthalpies I₁, I₂ and I₃ of four atoms with atomic numbers n, n + 1, n + 2 and n + 3, where n < 10, are tabulated below. What is the value of n? [JEE Adv 2020]
Atomic number | I₁ (kJ/mol) | I₂ (kJ/mol) | I₃ (kJ/mol)
n | 1681 | 3374 | 6050
n + 1 | 2081 | 3952 | 6122

s: For n + 2, I₂≫I₁ (alkali metal); for n + 3, I₃≫I₂ (alkaline earth metal). So n + 1 is a noble gas and n is a halogen. n < 10 gives n = 9 (F: 1681; Ne: 2081; Na: 496; Mg: 738).
